I read the whole file. I also read the simp attributes in Semiconj/Defs.lean: mul_right, one_right, one_left, pow_right and conj_iff are simp, and semiconjBy_iff_eq is simp for cancellative commutative monoids. I grepped Mathlib for other uses of these names.

The simp set in this file is as follows.
- `inv_inv_symm_iff` rewrites `SemiconjBy a⁻¹ x⁻¹ y⁻¹` to `SemiconjBy a y x`. It is simp at DivisionMonoid level.
- `inv_symm_left_iff` rewrites `SemiconjBy a⁻¹ y x` to `SemiconjBy a x y`. It removes an inverse and does not reintroduce one.
- `inv_right_iff` rewrites `SemiconjBy a x⁻¹ y⁻¹` to `SemiconjBy a x y`.
- `zpow_right` is simp and parallels the existing simp lemma `pow_right`.

In a Group, `inv_inv_symm_iff` overlaps with `inv_right_iff` followed by `inv_symm_left_iff`. Both routes give `SemiconjBy a y x`, so the rules are confluent. Each step strictly removes an inverse, so I see no credible cycle.

I did not find a missing canonical simp lemma, a wrong orientation, or unwanted expansion. `eq_one_iff` has a hypothesis and an explicit variable `a`, so it is correctly not simp. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out subtle simp-set interactions elsewhere in Mathlib.
